newsitem.title: USA: Qatar urges Clinton to relax Iran-Iraq containment. [CORRECTED 17:54 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Qatar urges Clinton to relax Iran-Iraq containment. [CORRECTED 17:54 GMT]

text.p: President Bill Clinton was urged by the Emir of Qatar on Wednesday to relax the U.S. strategy of "dual containment" of Iraq and Iran but was rebuffed.
The Emir of the small Gulf state, Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa al-Thani, raised the point in an Oval Office meeting with Clinton.

Afterward, both sides said the two leaders agreed to disagree. Clinton considers Iran a state sponsor of terrorism and Iraq a regional bully that refuses to abide by post-Gulf War U.N. resolutions at the expense of its own people.
The Emir told the Washington Post in an interview published on Wednesday that he could not endorse the "dual containment" strategy of Qatar's two neighbours.
He said Iran's election of a moderate, Mohammad Khatami (corrects name from Muhammad Khatemi and throughout the text), meant the United States had "no more excuses" for its policy toward Iran.

"The new president, Khatami, I think he is not from the extremists. I believe that communication with Iran is better for the United States and better for the area. Iran is a major country. You tried blocking Iran (economically), but you couldn't make it," the Emir said.

On Iraq, the Emir said: "I think the Iraqi people have suffered enough" because of U.N. sanctions. He stopped short of saying sanctions should be lifted, but said "the regime (of President Saddam Hussein) is more strong than before, so America should find a way."

The Emir's foreign minister, Sheikhh Hamad bin Jassim bin Jabr al-Thani, said the Emir discussed his ideas with Clinton and Clinton respected his views. He acknowledged the two leaders had "different opinions" on the subject.
White House spokesman Mike McCurry said Washington was sticking with "dual containment."

"We think our strategy for bringing international communities' concerns to bear on both countries in separate fashions, but in a way that demonstrates they are isolated from the internatioanl community because of their reprehensible policies, is a correct one," McCurry said.
McCurry said on Iran's election, "what matters are whether or not policies change."

"State sponsorship of terrorism and support for terrorism is a fundamental concern of the United States with respect to Iran, and that must change if there is going to be any change in the climate of relations," he said.
McCurry said Iraq deserved to be isolated because from time to time it "wantonly violates" the U.N. sanctions.

The Emir also discussed with Clinton a November regional economic summit conference in his capital, Doha. The Emir's foreign minister said the Emir did not raise whether he planned to invite Clinton to attend, but U.S. officials said they understood Qatar would like Clinton to go.
They also discussed the stalled Middle East peace process.
At the start of a meeting with Defence Secretary William Cohen, the Emir said Qatar had taken special precautions to safeguard U.S. forces, notably an Air Expeditionary Force, stationed there.
"With this in mind, it is also my goal to identify further opportunities to share defence intelligence on security threats in the region," Hamad said through a translator.
